title: Nordic stripe lap throw
subtitle: A 100 by 120 cm lap throw in bold multi-colour garter stripes, aran weight.
excerpt: A 100 by 120 cm lap throw in aran weight on 5 mm needles, worked in bold garter stripes: four rows each of five colours in a repeating palette sequence. Colours are carried up the left edge within each round; tails are minimal. About 350 g of each of three colours and 150 g each of two accent colours.
sourceNotes: Weldon's Practical Knitter, 8th series (1892), §Scandinavian Stripe Wraps, documents multi-colour garter stripe throws in aran weight as a fast lap-rug knitting project. The carry-up-the-side technique for five colours is described in the same source.

knitting.gaugeText: 18 sts × 36 rows = 10 × 10 cm in garter stitch on 5 mm needles, unblocked.

glossaryTerms.definition: A technique for managing yarn in stripe knitting. Instead of cutting the yarn at each colour change, the unused colours are carried loosely up the side edge of the work. On the first row of a new colour, the carried yarns are twisted with the active yarn at the edge to anchor them. Works cleanly for stripes of four rows or fewer.

content.text: A single-panel rectangle worked flat on 5 mm needles. Five colours stripe in bold garter sections. All colours are
carried up the side
throughout. Finished size: 100 cm wide by 120 cm long.

Single-panel construction, no seaming. Aran weight was chosen because the bold colours read better at a larger stitch size, the throw works up faster than DK, and the striped structure requires no cable needles, yarn-overs, or decreases. Carry all five colours up the left edge: at four rows per stripe in a five-colour sequence, each colour is at the edge every 20 rows, which is within the clean carry limit. Budget about 350 g each of three main colours and 150 g each of two accent colours.

content.text: Gauge
18 stitches and 36 rows to 10 cm in garter stitch on 5 mm needles. Swatch in one colour only; the stripe sequence does not affect gauge. At 36 rows per 10 cm the throw needs 432 rows to reach 120 cm.

If your stitch gauge is 16 per 10 cm with 180 stitches, the throw will be about 113 cm wide. Adjust cast-on by adding or removing a complete 20-row colour repeat (20 rows = 5 colours × 4 rows each) proportionally.
Stitches used

items.name: Yarns A, E
items.qty: five colours in sequence A, B, C, D, E, A, B, C, D, E ...

content.text: Pattern
Cast-on
Using Yarn A and the long-tail cast-on, cast on 180 stitches. Long-tail tail: (5 × 180) / 10 + 15 = 90 + 15 = 105 cm. Measure 120 cm of tail.
Body
Work 4 rows with Yarn A (knit every row). Twist Yarn B loosely around Yarn A at the left edge on rows 1 and 3 to anchor it.

Work 4 rows Yarn B, 4 rows Yarn C, 4 rows Yarn D, 4 rows Yarn E. Repeat the 20-row sequence until the throw measures 120 cm. Always change colours at the same edge. Twist the upcoming colour loosely every 2 rows at the edge to prevent long floats on the selvedge.
When you set this aside, note which colour is on the needle and which of the four rows within that stripe you are on.
Stitch count check-ins
At row 216 (about 60 cm): count across. You should have 180 stitches. At row 430 (about 119 cm): count again before casting off.
Common faults

Long floats looping off the side edge between colour sections: the carried yarns were not twisted every 2 rows. Even in a pure stripe project, loop lengths beyond about 3 cm at the selvedge will catch on items placed on the throw.
Colour sequence errors losing the palette rhythm: one stripe ran 5 or 6 rows instead of 4. Count rows within each stripe with a small tally mark on a sticky note until the 20-row rhythm is automatic.
Cast-off
Using whichever colour is active at 120 cm, cast off knitwise with a relaxed tension.
Finishing
Weave in the cast-on and cast-off ends only (the carried colours have no loose tails mid-work if the carry-up method was used throughout). Weave each end along a garter ridge on the wrong side.
Care
Machine wash on a gentle 30-degree cycle for superwash aran. Lay flat to dry. Check that all colours are colourfast before washing different coloured aran yarns together the first time.
What to try next

From bold garter stripes, the progression is a stranded colourwork throw: two colours worked simultaneously on each row to form geometric patterns. The same aran weight and needles apply; the new skill is managing two yarns on each row without tangling.
